title: Recovery and Discipleship
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Recovery and discipleship teaches that true restoration is more than stopping destructive behavior; it is learning to follow Jesus as a restored disciple. Recovery must be shaped by repentance, grace, truth, community, obedience, and hope in Christ.
summary: Recovery and discipleship teaches that true restoration is more than stopping destructive behavior; it is learning to follow Jesus as a restored disciple. Recovery must be shaped by repentance, grace, truth, community, obedience, and hope in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ does not merely remove chains; He calls restored people to follow Him. In Him, recovery becomes a pathway of discipleship, new identity, and growing obedience.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Recovery can be reduced to behavior change, sobriety milestones, or avoiding consequences. While those may matter, biblical restoration goes deeper. God calls people into life with Christ.

Discipleship addresses worship, identity, desires, habits, relationships, truth, repentance, and obedience. A person recovering from bondage needs more than abstinence; he needs to be formed as a follower of Jesus.

Grace trains believers to renounce ungodliness and live in a new way. Recovery is not self-salvation, but the ongoing work of God as people learn to walk in truth and freedom.

The church has a role in recovery by providing Scripture, prayer, accountability, encouragement, correction, patience, and belonging. Restoration is often walked out in community, not isolation.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People can stop one behavior while remaining spiritually lost, prideful, ashamed, or enslaved to another idol. Recovery without discipleship can leave the heart unchanged.

This doctrine keeps Restored Daily’s recovery focus anchored in Christ. The goal is not merely a cleaner life, but a restored life under the lordship and grace of Jesus.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pursue recovery as discipleship. Seek sobriety and freedom, but also pursue Scripture, prayer, repentance, worship, community, service, and obedience. If helping others, point them to Christ as Savior and Lord, not merely to behavior management.
